title: Deuteronomy 25: Just Judgment, the Brother's Duty, and Amalek
body:
Read the chapter → [Deuteronomy 25](/bible/deuteronomy/25)

**[Deuteronomy 25:1-3](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v1)</sup> If there be a controversy between men, and they come unto judgment, that the judges may judge them; then they shall justify the righteous, and condemn the wicked.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v2)</sup> And it shall be, if the wicked man be worthy to be beaten, that the judge shall cause him to lie down, and to be beaten before his face, according to his fault, by a certain number.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v3)</sup> Forty stripes he may give him, and not exceed: lest, if he should exceed, and beat him above these with many stripes, then thy brother should seem vile unto thee.

- If there be a controversy between men, the judges justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; the wicked man worthy to be beaten was made to lie down and be beaten before the judge's face, according to his fault, by a certain number.
- Forty stripes may he give him, and not exceed, lest thy brother should seem vile unto thee. Paul recounted receiving that beating under this law.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Corinthians 11:24-25](/bible/2-corinthians/11#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/2-corinthians/11#v24)</sup> Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/2-corinthians/11#v25)</sup> Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

    Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one; Paul recounted how he was beaten.

**[Deuteronomy 25:4](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v4)</sup> Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn.

- Thou shalt not muzzle the ox when he treadeth out the corn: the corn is the reward for the ox.
- Paul applies this verse to how the elders are treated: let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine, for the labourer is worthy of his reward.
- Giving double honour is not just saying the words to the leadership; it is true respect and reverence toward the leadership that labours in this word and doctrine.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Timothy 5:17-18](/bible/1-timothy/5#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/1-timothy/5#v17)</sup> Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine.
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/1-timothy/5#v18)</sup> For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.

    The elders that labour in the word and doctrine are worthy of double honour, for thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn.

**[Deuteronomy 25:5-10](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v5)**

> <sup>[5](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v5)</sup> If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v6)</sup> And it shall be, that the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v7)</sup> And if the man like not to take his brother’s wife, then let his brother’s wife go up to the gate unto the elders, and say, My husband’s brother refuseth to raise up unto his brother a name in Israel, he will not perform the duty of my husband’s brother.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v8)</sup> Then the elders of his city shall call him, and speak unto him: and if he stand to it, and say, I like not to take her;
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v9)</sup> Then shall his brother’s wife come unto him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v10)</sup> And his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

- If brethren dwell together and one of them die and have no child, the wife of the dead was not to marry without unto a stranger; her husband's brother took her to wife, and the firstborn she bare succeeded in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel.
- Check this out: this is no longer the law, so do not try to use it as an excuse toward your brother's wife. It stood for the name not being put out because of the land inheritance in Israel.
- The man who refused was called before the elders; his brother's wife loosed his shoe from off his foot, spat in his face, and answered, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house; and his name was called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.

  Precepts:
  - **[Genesis 38:6-10](/bible/genesis/38#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/38#v6)</sup> And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name was Tamar.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/genesis/38#v7)</sup> And Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the Lord; and the Lord slew him.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/genesis/38#v8)</sup> And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother’s wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/genesis/38#v9)</sup> And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother’s wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/38#v10)</sup> And the thing which he did displeased the Lord: wherefore he slew him also.

    Onan refused to raise up seed to his brother Er, and the thing which he did displeased the Lord.
  - **[Ruth 3:10-13](/bible/ruth/3#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/ruth/3#v10)</sup> And he said, Blessed be thou of the Lord, my daughter: for thou hast shewed more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, inasmuch as thou followedst not young men, whether poor or rich.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/ruth/3#v11)</sup> And now, my daughter, fear not; I will do to thee all that thou requirest: for all the city of my people doth know that thou art a virtuous woman.
    >
    > <sup>[12](/bible/ruth/3#v12)</sup> And now it is true that I am thy near kinsman: howbeit there is a kinsman nearer than I.
    >
    > <sup>[13](/bible/ruth/3#v13)</sup> Tarry this night, and it shall be in the morning, that if he will perform unto thee the part of a kinsman, well; let him do the kinsman’s part: but if he will not do the part of a kinsman to thee, then will I do the part of a kinsman to thee, as the Lord liveth: lie down until the morning.

    Boaz answered Ruth that he would perform the kinsman's part, but there was a kinsman nearer than he.
  - **[Ruth 4:1-6](/bible/ruth/4#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/ruth/4#v1)</sup> Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spake came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/ruth/4#v2)</sup> And he took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sat down.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/ruth/4#v3)</sup> And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi, that is come again out of the country of Moab, selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ruth/4#v4)</sup> And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it beside thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/ruth/4#v5)</sup> Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/ruth/4#v6)</sup> And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.

    The nearer kinsman could not redeem it, lest he mar his own inheritance, and the right passed to Boaz.
  - **[Matthew 22:23-30](/bible/matthew/22#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/matthew/22#v23)</sup> The same day came to him the Sadducees, which say that there is no resurrection, and asked him,
    >
    > <sup>[24](/bible/matthew/22#v24)</sup> Saying, Master, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed unto his brother.
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/matthew/22#v25)</sup> Now there were with us seven brethren: and the first, when he had married a wife, deceased, and, having no issue, left his wife unto his brother:
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/matthew/22#v26)</sup> Likewise the second also, and the third, unto the seventh.
    >
    > <sup>[27](/bible/matthew/22#v27)</sup> And last of all the woman died also.
    >
    > <sup>[28](/bible/matthew/22#v28)</sup> Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven? for they all had her.
    >
    > <sup>[29](/bible/matthew/22#v29)</sup> Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God.
    >
    > <sup>[30](/bible/matthew/22#v30)</sup> For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.

    The Sadducees put to Christ the case of seven brethren who under this law took one wife.

**[Deuteronomy 25:17-19](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v17)</sup> Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v18)</sup> How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/deuteronomy/25#v19)</sup> Therefore it shall be, when the Lord thy God hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.

- Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt: he met thee by the way and smote the hindmost of thee, all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary, and he feared not God.
- Israel was later commanded through Samuel to repay it: I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not.
- At Rephidim, where Amalek first came and fought with Israel, the Lord told Moses to write this for a memorial in a book and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua, for the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation; and that war is still going on even to this day.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Samuel 15:2-3](/bible/1-samuel/15#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/15#v2)</sup> Thus saith the Lord of hosts, I remember that which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/15#v3)</sup> Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.

    I remember that which Amalek did to Israel; now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have.
  - **[Exodus 17:8](/bible/exodus/17#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/17#v8)</sup> Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.

    Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim.
  - **[Exodus 17:14-16](/bible/exodus/17#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/17#v14)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/17#v15)</sup> And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/17#v16)</sup> For he said, Because the Lord hath sworn that the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

    Write this for a memorial in a book, for the Lord will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.
